pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Home
pageCache.text:
Welcome
Amazing Things Happen Here ... Brimpton Church of England Primary School serves the villages of Brimpton, Midgham, Crookham Common and the surrounding area. The school has strong links with the Parish Church and the local community. Founded in 1844 with land donated by the Earl of Falmouth, Brimpton School was rebuilt and enlarged in 1861. By 1900 the school had become a National School with places for 94 Scholars and by the 1950's the school was extended to provide the present accommodation.

There are currently no upcoming events.

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Mrs Z Baker Religious Education
pageCache.text:
Mrs Z Baker Religious Education
A Brimpton Theologian
Recognizes and retells simple accounts of core beliefs
Show an understanding and acceptance of a range of religious practices from around the world.
Reflects on issues affecting society in the modern world.
Can form and share their own opinions and respect those of others.
Will identify, investigate and respond to a variety of issues sensitively and responsibly.
Social, Moral, spiritual and Cultural (SMSC) values are embedded in RE and across the school curriculum allowing Children to develop positive attitudes and values through personal growth
Curriculum Subjects

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Mrs H Davies Music
pageCache.text:
Mrs H Davies Music
Creates original, imaginative and fluent compositions and performances.
They show musical understanding underpinned by high levels of aural perception, internalisation and knowledge of music, including high or rapidly developing levels of technical expertise.
They have an excellent understanding of how musical traditions and genres - the historical, social and cultural origins of music - contribute to the diversity of musical styles.
They give precise written and verbal explanations, using musical terminology effectively, accurately and appropriately.
Curriculum Subjects

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Mrs Z Baker Geography
pageCache.text:
Mrs Z Baker Geography
A Brimpton Geographer
Will have experiences of Geography to inspire and ignite their curiosity about the wider world.
Will be able to express opinions that are justified and reasoned through good knowledge around issues in society and the environment.
Can apply creativity, critical thinking and curiosity to give reasoned views on places, fieldwork and features of the world around us.
Will be able to enquire, question, analyse and present geographical concepts.
Will have the opportunity to develop an ability to explore and enquire geographical skills and techniques through fieldwork i.e. map skills.
Will develop a passion and a real sense of curiosity for the world and the people who live there and through SMSC will gain the skills to become a good global citizen.
To develop a sense of own location in relation to the rest of the world.
Curriculum Subjects

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Mrs Z Baker History
pageCache.text:
Mrs Z Baker History
A Brimpton Historian
Encompasses spiritual, moral, social and cultural development.
Acts like a good detective, is curious and ask important questions.
Will look for evidence at to find answers from artefacts or objects made by people in the past.
Has an enthusiastic engagement in learning, which develops their sense of curiosity about the past and their understanding of how and why people interpret the past in different ways.
Will develop knowledge and understanding of people, events, and contexts from a range of historical periods and of historical concepts and processes.
The ability to think, reflect, debate, discuss and evaluate the past, formulating and refining questions and lines of enquiry.
Will show respect for historical evidence and the ability to make robust and critical use of it to support their explanations and judgments.
Curriculum Subjects

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Mr N O'Connell Maths
pageCache.text:
Mr N O'Connell Maths
A Brimpton Mathematician
Learns new facts and skills to apply in mathematics.
Feels competent to use their mathematical skills across the curriculum.
Gives precise responses and explanations using mathematical vocabulary.
Attempts new challenges by using the skills they have previously learned.
Curriculum Subjects

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Art
pageCache.text:
Art
Designs and makes imaginative, creative, beautiful and/or thought-provoking artworks.
Is visually literate and increasingly able to communicate ideas through visual and tactile media.
Uses a variety of high-quality artist materials and natural and manmade resources to explore their knowledge and skills through hands on experience and is learning to make informed choices about the techniques and materials that they choose and use.
Experiences and explores a wide and diverse range of art works created by artists from different backgrounds, historical periods and cultures.
Is able to speak with confidence and enthusiasm about their own art work and the art work of others.
Is confident to try out different materials and techniques in a process driven rather than product lead way.
Values and respects their own art work and the art work of others.
Curriculum Subjects
Art

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - Design Technology
pageCache.text:
Design Technology
A Brimpton Design Technologist
Researches, plans, designs, makes and evaluates a variety of products using, textiles, food, 3D and technological media.
Can identify and evaluate existing design products and is aware of the role of designers and makers in society and of the impact of design on the environment and on daily life.
Has many, hands on opportunities to develop their practical skills and refine their designs.
Understands the value of trial and error and experimentation in the development of design.
Learns about design in different historical and cultural contexts and researches the contribution of designers and makers from diverse backgrounds.
Curriculum Subjects
Design Technology

pageCache.pageTitle: Brimpton Church of England Primary School - MFL
pageCache.text:
MFL
Will develop an enthusiastic and positive attitude to other languages and language learning.
Will make links between their own language and a Latin rooted language and become more aware of their own language(s) which will support their literacy and oracy in school.
Will develop a broader intercultural understanding and understand the world they live in better.
When leaving Brimpton CofE Primary School, children will have a natural curiosity and confidence to explore, other countries, cultures and languages. They will understand that, in a multi-lingual society it is important to be able to communicate effectively with others in another language. Children will be engaged and prepared to continue language learning at Secondary School.
Key Stage 2 pupils have started a pen pal correspondence with a French primary school Cloyes les Trois Rivieres in the region centre.
The children are using their French and English vocabulary to communicate with the children. They are learning about each other's culture and habits
Curriculum Subjects
